questions.prompt: Explain the three foundational themes of the Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Clarity, Deference, and Depth.
questions.modelAnswer: Clarity ensures text is legible at every size, icons are precise, and interactive elements are obvious to use. Deference means the user interface recedes into the background so that user content remains the primary focus. Depth uses visual layers, materials, shadows, and natural motion to convey hierarchy and spatial orientation across the application.

rubric.criterion: Defines Clarity as legible typography, precise iconography, and intuitive functionality.
Defines Deference as UI receding so content is the primary focus.
Defines Depth as using layers, shadows, and materials for spatial hierarchy.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Liquid Glass in Apple's design system, and where should it be applied?
questions.modelAnswer: Liquid Glass is a spatial material that combines frosted translucency with dynamic lighting and refraction. It allows underlying background colors and motion to peek through, giving users contextual awareness of their environment. According to Apple guidelines, Liquid Glass belongs exclusively on floating navigation chrome like toolbars, tab bars, and sheets, never over core body text.

rubric.criterion: Explains Liquid Glass is a translucent spatial material providing depth and contextual awareness.
Explains it belongs on navigation bars and floating chrome, never over core reading content.

questions.prompt: Why does Apple caution designers against stacking glass materials on top of other glass materials?
questions.modelAnswer: Stacking multiple translucent glass surfaces on top of each other compounds blur filters, creating visual noise and muddy color artifacts. This significantly degrades contrast and makes text and glyphs difficult to read. When placing interactive cards inside an already translucent container, developers should use opaque solid fills instead of nested glass.

rubric.criterion: Explains stacking glass causes visual noise, muddy colors, and loss of contrast.
Recommends using solid opaque colors for elements inside translucent containers.

questions.prompt: How does `UIVibrancyEffect` maintain legibility on top of blurred materials?
questions.modelAnswer: Blurred materials reflect the colors of content scrolling underneath them, which causes static gray or colored text to lose contrast and disappear. `UIVibrancyEffect` applies a dynamic color filter that pulls light through the material into foreground labels and icons. This automatically adjusts foreground contrast in real time so text stays legible regardless of background color shifts.

rubric.criterion: Explains static text disappears when underlying content colors change behind blurred materials.
Explains vibrancy filters light through the material to dynamically maintain contrast.

questions.prompt: How should an iOS app adapt when the user enables the Reduce Transparency accessibility setting?
questions.modelAnswer: When users enable Reduce Transparency in Settings, iOS removes blur effects to assist individuals with visual impairments or cognitive sensitivities. System components like toolbars convert automatically to solid backgrounds. Custom interface components must inspect `UIAccessibility.isReduceTransparencyEnabled` or the SwiftUI environment and replace translucent materials with high-contrast, opaque solid fills.

rubric.criterion: Explains Reduce Transparency assists low-vision users by removing blur and translucency.
Explains custom components must inspect the setting and render solid opaque backgrounds.
